verses.1:1: The word of the LORD which came to Hosea the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.
verses.1:2: When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of harlotry and children of harlotry, for the land utterly plays the harlot, departing from the LORD."
verses.1:3: Then he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore a son to him.
verses.1:4: And the LORD said to him, "Call his name Jezreel, for yet a little while, and I will avenge the bloodshed of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will bring to an end the kingdom of the house of Israel.
verses.1:5: And it shall be in that day that I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."
verses.1:6: And she conceived again and bore a daughter. Then He said to him, "Call her name Lo-Ruhamah, for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, that I should forgive them at all.
verses.1:7: Yet I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them by the LORD their God; and I will not save them by bow, or by sword, or by battle, by horses, or by horsemen."
verses.1:8: After she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, she conceived and bore a son.
verses.1:9: Then He said, "Call his name Lo-Ammi, for you are not My people, and I will not be yours."
verses.2:1: Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or numbered; and it shall be in the place where it is said to them, "You are not My people," there it shall be said to them, "Sons of the living God."
verses.2:2: Then the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head, and they shall go up out of the land; for great shall be the day of Jezreel.
verses.2:3: Say to your brothers, "My people," and to your sisters, "Shown mercy."
verses.2:4: Contend with your mother, contend! For she is not My wife, nor am I her husband. Let her put away her harlotries from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts;
verses.2:5: Lest I strip her naked and expose her as on the day she was born, and make her like a wilderness, and render her like a parched land, and slay her with thirst.
verses.2:6: And upon her children I will have no mercy, for they are children of harlotry.
verses.2:7: For their mother has played the harlot; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. For she said, "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my linen, my oil and my drink."
verses.2:8: Therefore, behold, I will hedge up your way with thorns, and I will raise a wall against her, so that she shall not find her paths.
verses.2:9: She shall pursue her lovers, yet she shall not overtake them; she shall seek them, yet she shall not find them. Then she shall say, "I will go and return to my first husband, for it was better for me then than now."
verses.2:10: And she did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil, and multiplied silver and gold for her, which they used for Baal.
verses.2:11: Therefore I will take back My grain in its time and My new wine in its season, and I will withdraw My wool and My linen, given to cover her nakedness.
verses.2:12: And now I will uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one shall deliver her out of My hand.
verses.2:13: I will also cause all her mirth to cease—her feasts, her New Moons, her Sabbaths, and all her appointed festivals.
verses.2:14: And I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, of which she said, "These are my wages that my lovers have given me." And I will make them a forest, and the beasts of the field shall devour them.
verses.2:15: I will punish her for the days of the Baals, when she burned incense to them, adorned herself with her rings and her jewelry, and went after her lovers; and Me she forgot, declares the LORD.
verses.2:16: Therefore, behold, I will allure her, lead her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.
verses.2:17: And from there I will give her her vineyards, and the Valley of Achor as a door of hope; and there she shall answer as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.2:18: And it shall come to pass in that day, declares the LORD, that you will call Me "My Husband," and will no longer call Me "My Master."
verses.2:19: For I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they shall no more be remembered by their name.
verses.2:20: And in that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, with the birds of the heavens, and with the creeping things of the ground; and I will break the bow, the sword, and war from the land, and I will make them lie down in safety.
verses.2:21: And I will betroth you to Myself forever; I will betroth you to Myself in righteousness and in justice, in lovingkindness and in mercy.
verses.2:22: I will betroth you to Myself in faithfulness, and you shall know the LORD.
verses.2:23: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will answer, declares the LORD; I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth.
verses.2:24: And the earth shall answer the grain, the new wine, and the oil; and they shall answer Jezreel.
verses.2:25: And I will sow her for Myself in the land; and I will have mercy on Lo-Ruhamah, and I will say to Lo-Ammi, "You are My people," and he shall say, "My God."
verses.3:1: Then the LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by a lover and is an adulteress, even as the LORD loves the children of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love raisin cakes."
verses.3:2: So I bought her for myself for fifteen shekels of silver, and a homer of barley and a lethek of barley.
verses.3:3: And I said to her, "You shall abide for me many days; you shall not play the harlot, nor shall you belong to a man; and so shall I also be toward you."
verses.3:4: For the children of Israel shall abide many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, without ephod or teraphim.
verses.3:5: Afterward the children of Israel shall return and seek the LORD their God and David their king, and they shall come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the latter days.
verses.4:1: Hear the word of the LORD, O children of Israel, for the LORD has a controversy with those who dwell in the land, because there is no truth, and no lovingkindness, and no knowledge of God in the land.
verses.4:2: Swearing and lying, murdering, stealing, and committing adultery—they break out, and bloodshed touches bloodshed.
verses.4:3: Therefore the land shall mourn, and everyone who dwells in it shall languish, along with the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens; even the fish of the sea shall be taken away.
verses.4:4: Yet let no man contend, and let no man reprove, for your people are like those who strive with a priest.
verses.4:5: So you shall stumble by day, and the prophet also shall stumble with you by night; and I will destroy your mother.
verses.4:6: My people are cut off for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from serving as priest to Me; and since you have forgotten the law of your God, I too will forget your children.
verses.4:7: The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me; I will exchange their glory for shame.
verses.4:8: They feed upon the sin of My people, and direct their desire toward their iniquity.
verses.4:9: And it shall be: like people, like priest. I will visit his ways upon him, and repay him for his deeds.
verses.4:10: They shall eat, yet not be satisfied; they shall play the harlot, yet not increase, because they have ceased to heed the LORD.
verses.4:11: Harlotry, wine, and new wine take away the understanding.
verses.4:12: My people inquire of their piece of wood, and their staff declares to them; for a spirit of harlotry has led them astray, and they have played the harlot, departing from their God.
verses.4:13: Upon the tops of the mountains they offer sacrifices, and upon the hills they burn incense, beneath oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. Therefore your daughters play the harlot, and your brides commit adultery.
verses.4:14: I will not punish your daughters when they play the harlot, nor your brides when they commit adultery; for the men themselves turn aside with harlots, and offer sacrifices with shrine prostitutes. Thus a people without understanding shall come to ruin.
verses.4:15: Though you play the harlot, O Israel, do not let Judah become guilty; do not come to Gilgal, nor go up to Beth-aven, nor swear, "As the LORD lives!"
verses.4:16: For like a stubborn heifer, Israel has become stubborn; now shall the LORD pasture them like a lamb in an open meadow?
verses.4:17: Ephraim is bound to idols; leave him alone.
verses.4:18: When their carousing is over, they continually play the harlot; her rulers dearly love shame.
verses.4:19: A wind has bound her up in its wings, and they shall be put to shame because of their sacrifices.
verses.5:1: Hear this, O priests! Pay attention, O house of Israel! And give ear, O house of the king! For the judgment is against you, because you have been a snare at Mizpah and a net spread out upon Tabor.
verses.5:2: The revolters have gone deep in slaughter, yet I am a chastisement to them all.
verses.5:3: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from Me; for now, O Ephraim, you have played the harlot, and Israel is defiled.
verses.5:4: Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God, for a spirit of harlotry is in their midst, and they do not know the LORD.
verses.5:5: The pride of Israel testifies against him to his face; therefore Israel and Ephraim shall stumble in their iniquity, and Judah also shall stumble with them.
verses.5:6: With their flocks and with their herds they shall go to seek the LORD, yet they shall not find Him; He has withdrawn Himself from them.
verses.5:7: They have dealt treacherously against the LORD, for they have borne illegitimate children. Now a month shall devour them together with their portions.
verses.5:8: Blow the ram's horn in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah! Sound the alarm at Beth-aven: "Behind you, O Benjamin!"
verses.5:9: Ephraim shall become a desolation in the day of rebuke; among the tribes of Israel I have declared what is sure.
verses.5:10: The princes of Judah have become like those who move a boundary stone; upon them I will pour out My wrath like water.
verses.5:11: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because he willingly followed a human precept.
verses.5:12: Therefore I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like rottenness to the house of Judah.
verses.5:13: When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah saw his wound, then Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to King Jareb; yet he is not able to heal you, nor can he cure your wound.
verses.5:14: For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, even I, will tear in pieces and depart; I will carry away, and none shall rescue.
verses.5:15: I will depart and return to My place, until they acknowledge their guilt and seek My face; in their affliction they will earnestly seek Me.
verses.6:1: Come, let us return to the LORD; for He Himself has torn, and He will heal us; He has struck, and He will bind us up.
verses.6:2: After two days He will restore us to life; on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live before Him.
verses.6:3: Let us know, let us press on to know the LORD! His coming forth is as sure as the dawn; He shall come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.
verses.6:4: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah? For your lovingkindness is like a morning cloud, and like the dew that vanishes early.
verses.6:5: Therefore I have hewn them down by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth, and your judgments go forth as the light.
verses.6:6: For I delight in lovingkindness and not sacrifice, and in the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
verses.6:7: Yet like Adam they have transgressed the covenant; there they have dealt treacherously against Me.
verses.6:8: Gilead is a city of workers of iniquity, tracked with blood.
verses.6:9: As bands of robbers lie in wait for a man, so the company of priests murder along the road to Shechem; for they have committed villainy.
verses.6:10: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: there is harlotry in Ephraim; Israel is defiled.
verses.6:11: Also, O Judah, a harvest is appointed for you, when I restore the fortunes of My people.
verses.7:1: When I would heal Israel, then the iniquity of Ephraim is uncovered, and the evil deeds of Samaria; for they deal in falsehood: a thief enters in, and a band of raiders plunders outside.
verses.7:2: And they do not consider in their heart that I remember all their wickedness; now their own doings encompass them; they are before My face.
verses.7:3: With their wickedness they gladden a king, and with their lies, princes.
verses.7:4: All of them are adulterers; they are like an oven blazing from a baker, who ceases from stirring the fire from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.
verses.7:5: On the day of our king, the princes grew sick with the heat of wine; he stretched out his hand with scoffers.
verses.7:6: For they bring their heart near like an oven while they lie in wait; all the night their baker sleeps, and in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
verses.7:7: All of them grow hot like an oven, and they devour their judges; all their kings have fallen, yet there is none among them who calls to Me.
verses.7:8: Ephraim mixes himself among the peoples; Ephraim has become a cake not turned over.
verses.7:9: Strangers have consumed his strength, yet he does not know it; gray hairs also are sprinkled upon him, yet he does not know it.
verses.7:10: And the pride of Israel testifies to his face; yet they have not returned to the LORD their God, nor have they sought Him for all this.
verses.7:11: Ephraim has become like a silly dove, without understanding; they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.
verses.7:12: As they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like the birds of the heavens; I will chastise them according to the report to their congregation.
verses.7:13: Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me! Destruction to them, for they have transgressed against Me! Though I would redeem them, yet they have spoken lies against Me.
verses.7:14: They do not cry out to Me from their heart, when they wail upon their beds; for grain and new wine they gather together, yet they rebel against Me.
verses.7:15: Though I disciplined and strengthened their arms, yet they devise evil against Me.
verses.7:16: They return, yet not to the Most High; they are like a treacherous bow. Their princes shall fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue; this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt.
verses.8:1: Put the trumpet to your mouth! One swoops like an eagle upon the house of the LORD, because they have transgressed My covenant and rebelled against My law.
verses.8:2: To Me they cry out, "My God, we, Israel, know You!"
verses.8:3: Israel has cast off what is good; an enemy shall pursue him.
verses.8:4: They set up kings, yet not from Me; they appointed princes, yet I did not know it. From their silver and their gold they made idols for themselves, that they might be cut off.
verses.8:5: Your calf is spurned, O Samaria! My anger burns against them; how long shall they be incapable of innocence?
verses.8:6: For it is from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is not God. Surely the calf of Samaria shall be reduced to splinters.
verses.8:7: For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind. It has no standing grain; the sprout yields no meal; and even if it should yield, strangers shall swallow it up.
verses.8:8: Israel is swallowed up; now they have become among the nations like a vessel in which there is no delight.
verses.8:9: For they have gone up to Assyria, a wild donkey wandering alone by itself; Ephraim has hired lovers.
verses.8:10: Though they hire allies among the nations, now I will gather them together; and they shall writhe for a little while under the burden of the king of princes.
verses.8:11: Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, they have become to him altars for sinning.
verses.8:12: Were I to write for him the myriads of My law, they are counted as a strange thing.
verses.8:13: As for the sacrifices of My offerings, they sacrifice flesh and eat it, yet the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins; they shall return to Egypt.
verses.8:14: For Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces, and Judah has multiplied fortified cities; yet I will send fire upon his cities, and it shall devour her citadels.
verses.9:1: Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the peoples, for you have played the harlot, departing from your God; you have loved a harlot's hire upon all the threshing floors of grain.
verses.9:2: The threshing floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the new wine shall fail her.
verses.9:3: They shall not dwell in the land of the LORD; instead, Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and in Assyria they shall eat what is unclean.
verses.9:4: They shall not pour out wine to the LORD, nor shall they be pleasing to Him. Their sacrifices shall be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat of it shall be defiled. For their bread shall be for their own appetite; it shall not come into the house of the LORD.
verses.9:5: What will you do on the day of the appointed assembly, and on the day of the feast of the LORD?
verses.9:6: For behold, they have departed because of destruction; Egypt shall gather them, and Memphis shall bury them. Nettles shall inherit the precious things of their silver; thorns shall be in their tents.
verses.9:7: The days of visitation have come; the days of recompense have come; Israel shall know it! The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad, because of the greatness of your iniquity, and great is the hostility.
verses.9:8: The watchman of Ephraim is with my God; yet the prophet is a fowler's snare upon all his ways, and hostility is in the house of his God.
verses.9:9: They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their iniquity, He will punish their sins.
verses.9:10: Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like the earliest fruit on the fig tree in its first season I saw your fathers. Yet they came to Baal-Peor and consecrated themselves to shame, and they became detestable things like what they loved.
verses.9:11: As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird—no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.
verses.9:12: Though they raise their children, yet I will bereave them until not a man is left; yes, woe to them also when I depart from them!
verses.9:13: Ephraim, as I saw Tyre, is planted in a pleasant meadow; yet Ephraim must bring out his sons to the slayer.
verses.9:14: Give them, O LORD—what will You give? Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts!
verses.9:15: All their wickedness is in Gilgal, for there I hated them. Because of the evil of their deeds I will drive them out of My house. I will love them no more; all their princes are rebels.
verses.9:16: Ephraim is stricken, their root is dried up; they shall yield no fruit. Even though they give birth, yet I will slay the precious offspring of their womb.
verses.9:17: My God will cast them away, because they have not listened to Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations.
verses.10:1: Israel is a luxuriant vine; he yields fruit for himself. According to the abundance of his fruit he multiplied altars; according to the goodness of his land they made fine sacred pillars.
verses.10:2: Their heart is divided; now they shall bear their guilt. He will break down their altars; He will ruin their sacred pillars.
verses.10:3: For now they shall say, "We have no king, because we did not fear the LORD; and as for the king, what can he do for us?"
verses.10:4: They speak mere words, swearing falsely in making a covenant; therefore judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of the field.
verses.10:5: The inhabitants of Samaria shall fear for the calves of Beth Aven; indeed, its people mourn over it, and its idolatrous priests tremble over it—over its glory, because it has departed into exile from it.
verses.10:6: It also shall be carried to Assyria as tribute to King Jareb. Ephraim shall receive shame, and Israel shall be ashamed of his own counsel.
verses.10:7: As for Samaria, her king is cut off like a twig upon the face of the waters.
verses.10:8: The high places of Aven, the sin of Israel, shall also be destroyed; the thorn and thistle shall grow up upon their altars. And they shall say to the mountains, "Cover us!" and to the hills, "Fall on us!"
verses.10:9: From the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel; there they stood. Shall not war overtake them in Gibeah against the sons of iniquity?
verses.10:10: When I desire, I will chasten them; and peoples shall be gathered against them when they are bound for their two iniquities.
verses.10:11: Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh, and I passed over her fair neck; now I will harness Ephraim, Judah shall plow, and Jacob shall break his clods.
verses.10:12: Sow for yourselves in righteousness; reap according to lovingkindness; break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, until He comes and rains righteousness upon you.
verses.10:13: You have plowed wickedness; you have reaped iniquity; you have eaten the fruit of falsehood, because you trusted in your own way, in the multitude of your mighty men.
verses.10:14: Therefore a tumult shall arise among your people, and all your fortresses shall be despoiled, as Shalman despoiled Beth Arbel in the day of battle—the mother was dashed in pieces with her children.
verses.10:15: Thus shall Bethel do to you because of the evil of your wickedness; at dawn the king of Israel shall surely be cut off.
verses.11:1: When Israel was a youth, then I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son.
verses.11:2: As they called to them, so they went away from them; they sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
verses.11:3: Yet I Myself taught Ephraim to walk; He took them up in His arms, yet they did not know that I healed them.
verses.11:4: I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love; and I was to them as those who lift the yoke from their jaws, and I bent down to him and fed him.
verses.11:5: He shall not return to the land of Egypt, but Assyria shall be his king, because they refused to return.
verses.11:6: And the sword shall whirl through his cities, and shall consume his gate bars and devour them because of their own counsels.
verses.11:7: My people are bent on turning away from Me. Though they call them to the Most High, none at all will exalt Him.
verses.11:8: How can I give you up, O Ephraim? How can I hand you over, O Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I set you like Zeboiim? My heart turns within Me; all My compassions are kindled together.
verses.11:9: I will not execute the fierceness of My anger; I will not return to destroy Ephraim. For I am God, and not man, the Holy One in your midst; and I will not come in wrath.
verses.11:10: They shall walk after the LORD; He will roar like a lion. When He roars, then the children shall come trembling from the west.
verses.11:11: They shall come trembling like a bird from Egypt, and like a dove from the land of Assyria; and I will cause them to dwell in their houses, says the LORD.
verses.12:1: Ephraim has encompassed Me with falsehood, and the house of Israel with deceit; yet Judah still walks with God, and is faithful with the Holy One.
verses.12:2: Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind; all the day long he multiplies falsehood and violence. They make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried to Egypt.
verses.12:3: The LORD also has a controversy with Judah, and He will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds He will repay him.
verses.12:4: In the womb he grasped his brother by the heel, and in his vigor he strove with God.
verses.12:5: Yes, he strove with the Angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded with Him. At Bethel He found him, and there He spoke with us.
verses.12:6: Even the LORD, the God of hosts—the LORD is His memorial.
verses.12:7: Therefore you, return to your God; observe lovingkindness and justice, and wait upon your God continually.
verses.12:8: A merchant—in his hand are scales of deceit; he loves to oppress.
verses.12:9: And Ephraim has said, "Surely I have become rich; I have found wealth for myself. In all my labors they shall find in me no iniquity that is sin."
verses.12:10: Yet I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.
verses.12:11: I have also spoken to the prophets, and I have multiplied visions; and by the hand of the prophets I have given parables.
verses.12:12: If Gilead is iniquity, surely they have become worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; indeed, their altars shall be like heaps of stones upon the furrows of the field.
verses.12:13: Now Jacob fled to the country of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept flocks.
verses.12:14: By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was kept.
verses.12:15: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger; therefore He will leave his bloodguilt upon him, and his Lord will repay him for his reproach.
verses.13:1: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he exalted himself in Israel. Yet through Baal he incurred guilt, and he died.
verses.13:2: And now they sin even more, and have made for themselves a molten image from their silver, idols according to their own skill, all of it the work of craftsmen. Concerning them they say, "Let the men who offer sacrifice kiss the calves!"
verses.13:3: Therefore they shall be like the morning cloud and like the early dew that quickly passes away, like chaff driven by a whirlwind from a threshing floor, and like smoke from a chimney.
verses.13:4: Yet I am the LORD your God since the land of Egypt; you shall know no God besides Me, and there is no savior apart from Me.
verses.13:5: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of scorching drought.
verses.13:6: According to their pasture they were satisfied; they were filled, and their heart was lifted up; therefore they forgot Me.
verses.13:7: So I will be to them like a lion; like a leopard beside the road I will lie in wait.
verses.13:8: I will confront them like a bear bereaved of her cubs, and I will tear open the enclosure of their heart; there I will devour them like a fierce lion, and the wild beast of the field shall rip them apart.
verses.13:9: O Israel, you are destroyed, for you are against Me, against your help.
verses.13:10: Where now is your king, that he may save you in all your cities? And where are your judges, of whom you said, "Give me a king and princes"?
verses.13:11: I gave you a king in My anger, and took him away in My wrath.
verses.13:12: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored away.
verses.13:13: The pangs of a woman in childbirth come upon him; he is an unwise son, for when the time arrives he does not present himself at the opening of the womb.
verses.13:14: From the hand of Sheol I will ransom them; from death I will redeem them. Where are your plagues, O Death? Where is your destruction, O Sheol? Compassion shall be hidden from My eyes.
verses.13:15: Though he may flourish among his brethren, an east wind shall come, the wind of the LORD ascending from the wilderness; his spring shall dry up, and his fountain shall become parched. It shall plunder the treasury of every precious vessel.
verses.14:1: Samaria shall bear her guilt, for she has rebelled against her God. They shall fall by the sword; their little ones shall be dashed in pieces, and their pregnant women shall be ripped open.
verses.14:2: Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled through your iniquity.
verses.14:3: Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to Him, "Take away all iniquity, and accept what is good, and we will offer our lips as bulls.
verses.14:4: Assyria shall not save us; we will not ride on horses, nor will we say anymore, 'Our gods,' to the work of our hands; for in You the fatherless finds mercy."
verses.14:5: I will heal their apostasy; I will love them freely, for My anger has turned from him.
verses.14:6: I will be like the dew to Israel; he shall blossom like the lily and strike his roots like Lebanon.
verses.14:7: His tender shoots shall spread forth; his splendor shall be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.
verses.14:8: Those who dwell in his shadow shall return; they shall flourish like grain and blossom like the vine; his renown shall be like the wine of Lebanon.
verses.14:9: Ephraim shall say, "What more have I to do with idols?" It is I who have answered and will watch over him. I am like a luxuriant cypress tree; from Me your fruit is found.
verses.14:10: Who is wise, that he may understand these things? Who is discerning, that he may know them? For the ways of the LORD are upright; the righteous shall walk in them, yet transgressors shall stumble in them.

notes.1:4: The name Jezreel means "God sows" and recalls the bloody purge of Ahab's house carried out by Jehu at Jezreel (2 Kings 9-10).
notes.1:6: Lo-Ruhamah means "Not Shown Mercy." The closing Hebrew clause literally reads "for lifting I will lift for them," understood either as continuing the negation ("to forgive them at all") or adversatively ("but I will surely carry them away").
notes.1:9: Lo-Ammi means "Not My People." The final clause literally reads "and I will not be to you," echoing the divine covenant name "I AM" (Ehyeh) in Exodus 3:14.
notes.2:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew text, chapter 2 begins here; verses 2:1-25 correspond to 1:10-2:23 in most English versions.
notes.2:3: The Hebrew reads Ammi ("My people") and Ruhamah ("Shown mercy"), directly reversing the judgment names Lo-Ammi and Lo-Ruhamah in chapter 1.
notes.2:8: The Masoretic Hebrew shifts mid-verse from second-person address ("your way") to third-person ("her wall... her paths").
notes.2:17: The Valley of Achor means "Valley of Trouble" (Joshua 7:24-26). The Hebrew verb translated "answer" can also mean "sing," evoking Israel's song at the Exodus while anticipating the responsive chain in verses 23-24.
notes.2:18: The Hebrew plays on Ishi ("My Husband") and Baali ("My Master"), the latter sharing the name of the Canaanite deity Baal mentioned in the next verse.
notes.3:2: The Hebrew literally reads "fifteen of silver" (standard idiom for shekels). A homer was a large dry measure of roughly six bushels, and a lethek was half a homer.
notes.3:4: An ephod was a priestly vestment associated with seeking divine guidance, and teraphim were household idols or divinatory images.
notes.3:5: The Hebrew verb rendered "come trembling to" literally means "fear toward," expressing eager, reverent awe before the LORD.
notes.4:4: The Masoretic text reads literally "like those who contend with a priest," evoking the stubborn defiance of priestly judicial authority (cf. Deut. 17:12).
notes.4:6: Follows the Qere reading "and I will reject you"; the Ketiv contains an extra orthographic aleph with the same meaning.
notes.4:8: The Hebrew word for "sin" also denotes a "sin offering," underscoring the irony that the priests feed on the offerings for sin and thus desire the people's iniquity to increase.
notes.4:15: Beth-aven ("house of wickedness") is Hosea's scornful wordplay on Bethel ("house of God"), a prominent center of northern idolatrous worship.
notes.5:2: Follows the Masoretic text literally ("in slaughter the revolters have gone deep"), referring to deep entanglement in bloodshed or idolatrous sacrifices.
notes.5:7: Hebrew chodesh means both "month" (indicating sudden ruin) and "New Moon" (implying that their own festival observances will consume their heritage).
notes.5:11: Hebrew tsav ("precept" or "command") likely refers to the unauthorized cultic ordinances established in the northern kingdom.
notes.5:13: "King Jareb" is a Hebrew epithet meaning "King Contender" (and perhaps a play on the Akkadian royal title for "the great king"), referring to the king of Assyria.
notes.6:3: The verb translated "waters" (yoreh) is also the Hebrew noun for the autumn or "early rain," evoking both the spring and autumn rains of the land.
notes.6:5: Follows the Masoretic text ("your judgments," that is, the verdicts pronounced against Israel and Judah) going forth clearly as the light.
notes.6:7: Hebrew ke-adam may mean "like Adam" or "like mortal men," and "there" points to the place of covenant unfaithfulness elaborated in the verses that follow.
notes.6:10: Follows the Qere reading sha'aruriyyah ("a horrible thing"), an orthographic variant of the Ketiv with the same sense.
notes.7:5: The Hebrew verb translated "grew sick" may also be rendered causatively, "made him sick," depicting court officials intoxicating the king during a conspiracy.
notes.7:12: "According to the report to their congregation" translates a compact Hebrew phrase referring to the covenant warnings publicly proclaimed to Israel's assembly.
notes.7:16: "Not to the Most High" renders the terse Hebrew expression lo al, literally "not upward" or "not to the One on high."
notes.8:10: The phrase "writhe for a little while" may also be read "begin to diminish"; "king of princes" reflects the Assyrian monarch's boastful royal title (cf. Isaiah 10:8).
notes.8:12: Translates the Masoretic qere readings ekhtav-lo ("I write for him") and rubbei ("myriads of"); the ketiv spells the verb plene and reads the singular rubbo ("a myriad").
notes.8:13: "My offerings" renders a rare reduplicated Hebrew noun derived from the root "to give," referring to sacrificial gifts brought to the sanctuary.
notes.9:2: The Hebrew shifts to the feminine singular "her," personifying Israel as the unfaithful wife addressed in verse 1.
notes.9:8: The Hebrew syntax of the opening clause is compressed and may also be understood as "Ephraim is a watchman with my God," contrasting true prophetic watchfulness with the snares laid against the prophet.
notes.9:10: "Shame" (boshet) is a polemical substitute for Baal, recalling Israel's apostasy at Baal-Peor in the wilderness (Numbers 25:1-5).
notes.9:16: Translates the Masoretic qere negative particle bal ("not"); the ketiv has the synonymous poetic negative beli.
notes.10:1: The Hebrew participle boqeq can mean either luxuriant or emptying; luxuriant fits the parallel clauses describing abundant fruit and a prosperous land.
notes.10:5: The Masoretic text uses the feminine plural calves alongside masculine singular pronouns referring back to the chief idol of Beth Aven, and the verb yagilu can mean either trembling in dread or former rejoicing.
notes.10:10: Following the Masoretic Qere onotam, their iniquities; the Ketiv eynotam reads their eyes or their furrows.
notes.11:2: The Masoretic Hebrew reads third-person plural, they called to them and from them, referring to the prophets whom the LORD sent to summon Israel.
notes.11:3: The Masoretic text shifts briefly from first person to third person in the middle clause, He took them up in His arms, before returning to first person.
notes.11:7: The difficult Hebrew phrase el-al is understood here as to the Most High, though it may also mean upward.
notes.11:9: The Hebrew be'ir can be rendered either in wrath and terror or into the city.
notes.12:1: Following the Masoretic Hebrew versification, where 12:1 corresponds to 11:12 in some English Bibles; qedoshim is a plural of majesty referring to the Holy One.
notes.12:5: The Masoretic text reads immanu, with us, uniting the later generation of Israel with the revelation given to Jacob at Bethel.
notes.12:8: The Hebrew word rendered merchant is Kena'an, Canaan, used idiomatically for a trader with ironic reference to Ephraim.
notes.13:2: The Hebrew construct phrase rendered "the men who offer sacrifice" can also be understood literally as "those who offer human sacrifices."
notes.13:9: The concise Hebrew wording of this verse is difficult and may also be rendered, "You are destroyed, O Israel, yet in Me is your help."
notes.13:10: The rare Hebrew form ehi (occurring here and in 13:14) functions as an interrogative meaning "Where?", though it is spelled like the verb "I will be."
notes.13:14: Although the opening two clauses lack an explicit interrogative particle in the Hebrew, they may also be read as rhetorical questions ("Shall I ransom them...?") leading into the refusal of compassion at the close of the verse.
notes.14:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew text, this verse begins chapter 14 (numbered as 13:16 in many English Bibles), so each following verse in chapter 14 is numbered one higher than in those editions.
notes.14:3: The Hebrew reads literally "we will render bulls, our lips," expressing verbal praise and confession offered in place of sacrificial bulls.
notes.14:9: The verb "shall say" is implied by the abrupt shift to Ephraim's renunciation of idols, which is immediately followed by the LORD's reply.
